papers.title_en: RecallFlow: Episodic Memory as the Source Distribution of Generative Robot Policies
papers.authors: Xuji Zhang, Qilin Zhong, Zichen Zhang, Wei Zhai, Jian Di, Kun Li, Yang Cao, Wenjun Lv
papers.evidence: 将情景记忆作为生成式机器人策略的源分布，实现记忆依赖操作。
papers.tldr: 在依赖记忆的机器人操作中，现有策略从高斯噪声开始生成动作，难以从冗长历史中定位相关目标，导致不可靠决策。RecallFlow从情景记忆构建源分布，通过Recall-Relocalization关联记忆与当前视图，Recall Anchors将记忆槽转为高斯分量，使生成从接近预期动作开始。在MIKASA-Robo基准上平均成功率达80.4%，在自建套件和真实机器人任务上分别比最强基线高20.3和18.8个百分点，显著提升记忆依赖操作性能且推理成本低。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion and flow-matching policies have become a standard choice for visuomotor imitation learning, owing to their ability to model multimodal action distributions. In memory-dependent manipulation, the robot must act on information that is no longer visible. Existing methods feed the observation history to the policy as an additional condition, while action generation still starts from Gaussian noise. However, the policy must then pick out the relevant target from a long and redundant history, leading to spurious correlations and unreliable decisions as the memory load grows. Additionally, the initial noise carries no information about what the robot has seen, leaving generation without guidance toward the remembered target. To address these issues, we propose RecallFlow, a flow-policy framework that builds the source distribution from episodic memory. Recall-Relocalization relates the memory to the current view through a few recall slots, so that the source reflects where the remembered targets are now. Recall Anchors then turns each slot into a Gaussian component of the source, enabling generation to start close to the intended action instead of from noise. The transport network then completes the action from the current observation alone, keeping inference nearly as cheap as a memoryless policy. We further build a suite of memory-dependent tasks grouped by memory load and compare all policies under a matched protocol. Extensive experiments show that RecallFlow achieves a state-of-the-art average success rate of 80.4% on the public MIKASA-Robo memory benchmark, and outperforms the strongest baseline by 20.3 points on our suite and by 18.8 points on four real-robot tasks.

papers.title_en: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
papers.authors: Kelvin Kiu-Wai Tam, Newt Hue-Nam K. Nguyen, Tianshi Zheng, Yunxiang Mo, Weihan Li, Zhongwei Xie, Chiu Yeung Tang, Jui-Yu Ho, Yangqiu Song, Ginny Y. Wong, Simon See
papers.evidence: 研究自动科研智能体的框架设计，关注上下文管理（保留）和技能管理（复用）。
papers.tldr: 自主研究智能体虽加速科研，但现有harness混合多种机制，难以厘清各组件作用。本研究从上下文管理与技能管理两个维度系统拆解设计，在MLE-Bench和KernelBench上评估。发现上下文折叠效果最佳，最高提升19.2%，选择性删除未用技能更优；结合两者提出MLEvolver，在MLE-Bench Lite奖牌率72.7%，KernelBench Level 3 fast1得分94%。该工作提炼出保留实验历史与整理经验的设计原则，推动自进化智能体持续进步。
papers.abstract_en: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each against a recency-truncation baseline within a shared agent framework. For context management, we find that preserving individually accessible records of past attempts is more effective than maintaining a rolling summary, with context folding performing best across all six settings and improving upon the baseline by up to 19.2%. For skill management, selectively discarding persistently unused lessons is more effective on average than consolidating them or promoting them to standing rules. Building on these findings, we combine context folding and skill deletion in MLEvolver, which achieves a 72.7% medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite and a 94% $\mathrm{fast}_1$ score on KernelBench Level 3, substantially outperforming AIDE and OpenEvolve under the same inference budget. Overall, our study distills design principles for preserving experimental history and curating reusable lessons in autoresearch harnesses, paving the way for agents that turn accumulated experience into sustained progress.

papers.title_en: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
papers.authors: Huanran Li, Nhat X. T. Le, Kevin De Angeli, Yao Xuan, Alireza Vahdatpour, Djordje Gligorijevic
papers.evidence: 提出Engram记忆系统，存储试验结果、假设和理由，供LLM智能体跨会话复用。
papers.tldr: LLM智能体调优神经网络时缺乏跨会话记忆，重复试错且异构模型间经验难复用。Engram多阶段记忆系统关联试验结果与假设及理由，在线智能体在初始引导、会话检索、候选审查三阶段提供适用证据，离线蒸馏验证经验实现自改进。在两个广告模型上，Engram达到无记忆对照32次试验效果仅需53%试验次数，且最终模型平均更优。该记忆机制为异构模型智能调优提供了可复用方案，显著降低成本并提升效果。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents can now tune neural networks, yet without cross-session memory they spend costly trials rediscovering known lessons. Reuse is difficult because production models differ in architecture, training setup and inference budget. We present Engram, a memory system that links past trial outcomes with the hypotheses and rationale behind them and assesses whether this evidence applies to the current model. An online agent curates evidence at the decision points where it is needed: Initial Guidance supplies validated lessons at the start, Session Retrieval supplies related past sessions before each batch of hypotheses is generated, and Trial Candidate Review checks each trial candidate against matching past trials. Between sessions, an offline agent distills validated lessons, making the memory self-improving. On two ads models, Engram reaches the 32-trial result of a no-memory control with 47% fewer trials and also ends with a better model on average.

papers.title_en: Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory
papers.authors: Tianmai M. Zhang, Hoda Shajari, Amr Hendy, Xiaohu Liu, Piyush Behre, Omar Zia Khan, Ankur Gupta
papers.evidence: 面向工具使用智能体持续适应的双极性记忆工作流
papers.tldr: 现有LLM智能体虽能利用程序性记忆从任务轨迹中自我改进，但局部成功与失败记忆的不同效用尚不明确。本文提出双极性记忆与定期维护方法DualPM，从每次轨迹的成功和失败中生成可定制反思与程序性记忆，并在长期任务流中周期性整合防止记忆膨胀。预quential评估显示失败记忆扩展覆盖，成功记忆精简执行，结合两者可兼具优势，支持跨域泛化与持续适应。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios. We develop \emph{Dual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance} (DualPM), a simple, retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. Online prequential evaluation with fine-grained metrics reveals that failure memory more strongly broadens coverage, success memory better streamlines execution, while combining both polarities effectively integrates both benefits. Further studies demonstrate that DualPM enables cross-domain memory generalization and continual memory adaptation, while external evaluation on EvoMemBench reveals the portability and effectiveness of DualPM as a general long-term procedural memory method.

papers.title_en: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
papers.authors: Yifei Xu, Li Yu, Zhaoyang Liu, Ce Wang, Sen Huang, Yanyan Shen, Yun Lin, Linpeng Huang, Hong Mei
papers.evidence: 面向AI助手记忆系统的评估驱动harness优化
papers.tldr: 针对长期AI助手内存系统harness优化仍依靠手工配置且缺乏结构性改进的现状，HoMe提出评估驱动的自动优化框架，通过迭代评估与编辑任意候选harness、结合会话级版本控制和执行轨迹定位共享失败机制，并利用候选门控、冒烟测试、自适应采样与记忆复用降低评估开销。在开源内存系统ReMe及LongMemEval-S、BEAM两个基准上，仅六次候选评估即超越原有强harness，同时大幅减少查询时token消耗，为实用化内存系统自动优化提供了可行路径。
papers.abstract_en: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. However, optimizing the harness of a memory system remains largely manual, and unrestricted editing alone does not ensure structural improvements. In this paper, we introduce HoMe, an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively evaluates candidate harnesses and derives each new candidate from any previously evaluated harness by editing any part of it. HoMe combines session-level memory versioning with execution traces to identify shared failure mechanisms across cases and localize them to the responsible sessions and harness components. It encourages early structural exploration through candidate gating and reduces evaluation cost through smoke tests, adaptive sampling, and the reuse of constructed memory. We validate HoMe with the open-source memory system ReMe on two large-scale long-horizon memory benchmarks, LongMemEval-S and BEAM. With six formal candidate evaluations per benchmark, after a full initial evaluation, HoMe discovers harnesses that improve end-task performance over the originally strong harness while consuming far fewer query-time tokens. The code is available at https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe.

papers.title_en: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
papers.evidence: 通过激活引导和知识编辑解决LLM智能体记忆幻觉
papers.tldr: 现有LLM智能体依赖外部记忆，但仍出现使用期幻觉：模型忽略检索到的正确记忆、误用于无关实体或混淆事实版本。TASK memory通过文本笔记、可移除知识编辑和一对引导向量共享同一模型内地址，逐查询控制记忆采用。在冻结模型上，TASK将记忆忽略幻觉降至1.5%以下，邻居误用从39.2%降至7.5%，在300/3000记忆库和事实修订及多跳任务上显著超越RAG和近期方法。该框架为克服记忆幻觉提供了可组合、可控的解决方案。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents increasingly rely on external memory, yet they still hallucinate about what they remember. Often the correct memory is retrieved and placed in the prompt, but the answer contradicts it or the memory is applied to the wrong question. We call these use-time memory hallucinations. Across five open models, we find that they arise from the conflict between parametric knowledge and external memory and take three forms: memory-ignoring, where the model returns to a stale fact in its weights (up to 46% of queries); memory-misapplying, where it attributes the memory to unrelated entities (up to 24%, and 49% when retrieval is combined with weight editing); and version confusion, where 53% of answers about revised facts assert the superseded value when both versions remain stored. We propose TASK memory, which goes beyond text-only memory by combining a Text note with Activation Steering and Knowledge editing that share one in-model address. The text holds the content. A removable knowledge edit supplies the address through its subject key and supports multi-hop composition. A pair of steering vectors decides, query by query, whether the model adopts the memory or keeps its own answer; the vectors store no content and control how the text memory is used. On frozen models under a pre-registered, test-once protocol, TASK reduces memory-ignoring hallucinations to at most 1.5% in all ten model-dataset cells and cuts neighbour misuse from 39.2% to 7.5% (+10.8 pp composite on CounterFact). It improves a 300-memory library over BM25 RAG by 16.4 pp, an advantage that holds at 3,000 memories, resolves fact revisions without fact IDs, and adds 7.5 pp of multi-hop accuracy on MQuAKE. 21 of 23 cross-model comparisons (8B-27B, four families) are significant, and TASK beats three recent context-steering methods in 9 of 10 model-dataset cells.

papers.title_en: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
papers.authors: Shaoteng Liu, Shuai Yang, Wei Huang, Luozhou Wang, Song Han, Yukang Chen
papers.evidence: 提出异步智能体记忆，用于长视频生成中保持实体一致性。
papers.tldr: 实时视频生成难以保持长故事中的人物、物体与地点一致性，离线 agent 记忆方案不适合直播流。Agentic LongLive 提出异步记忆 agent，仅依据已揭示提示维护实体文本与图像记忆，并预填充到生成器注意力。在 LongStory-Online 基准上，持久状态准确性提升 26.3 点，主角身份与地点一致性大幅提高，额外耗时约1%，系统可实时流式运行。这是首个由 LLM agent 维护记忆的实时视频生成器。
papers.abstract_en: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story. Agent systems provide such memory for offline multi-shot generation, yet they read the whole script in advance, plan each shot before generating it, and regenerate failed shots, which a live stream does not allow. We present Agentic LongLive, an asynchronous agentic memory for long video generation. A memory agent on separate GPUs reads only the prompts revealed so far, never the generated video, and keeps a text state and evolving images for every person, object, and scene. From this entity memory it composes a global image and a per-shot memory image, which an auxiliary GPU prefills into the generator's attention sink before the next shot starts, and writes entity cards for the prompts that name them, so the video never waits for memory and video errors are not written back. A small language model, trained with reinforcement learning and an image reward calibrated using downstream video outcomes, decides what to remember before the next prompt is known. On LongStory-Online, a new benchmark of 25 stories (857 shots) revealed one shot at a time, Agentic LongLive improves persistent-state accuracy of LongLive-2.0, its base generator, by 26.3 points, protagonist identity by 44.9, and revisited-place consistency by 40.4, at about 1% extra generation time on H100. The full system streams faster than real time on one 8xB200 node with the generator in BF16 (34.3 FPS), keeps image quality stable over 14-minute stories, and improves identity on two MiniMax-H3 generators, one of which, LongLive-H3, also runs in real time with it. To our knowledge, it is the first real-time video generator with text and image memory kept by an LLM agent.

papers.title_en: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Zilang Cen, Chao Tang, Fangcheng Liu, Weishi Mi, Wei Hao, JiaYu Xu, Dehao Huang, Yehui Tang, Xiaohui Cui, Tingguang Li, Xiaoyuan Zhang
papers.evidence: 利用有序交互记忆估计任务状态
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作依赖大模型推理，但频繁调用带来高延迟与 token 成本。本文提出 RoC 框架，通过在线任务状态监控器协调低层策略与高层推理代理，仅在需要时触发代理审查。该监控器结合时序视觉与交互记忆估计子任务进度并预测后继，实现执行修复与规划修订的联动。实验显示 RoC 在 RMBench 上成功率提升 24 个百分点、token 消耗降低 65.3%，并在真实任务中验证有效。
papers.abstract_en: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

papers.title_en: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
papers.authors: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li, Zhixiang Lu, Haolin Yang, Jianxu Chen, Yifan Lu, Di Fan, Yutong Xie
papers.evidence: 面向空间智能体的自进化框架，包含经验与技能记忆
papers.tldr: 针对空间推理智能体依赖外部工具但编排易重复出错的问题，SpatialCraft提出一种自进化框架，从交互历史中提取经验与技能而不更新模型参数。经验是条件-动作策略，技能是多步过程，通过对比效用评估将高效经验固化为技能。在五个空间基准和四个骨干模型上取得全部20个设置的最优准确率，证明冻结智能体可通过自身经验学会编排空间工具。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial reasoning agents increasingly rely on external tools, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation, to answer questions that a multimodal large language model (MLLM) cannot resolve from pixels alone. Tool access, however, shifts the bottleneck to orchestration: the agent must decide which tools to call, in what order, and how to interpret their outputs, yet a stateless agent repeats the same mistakes across tasks. We ask whether a frozen tool-using agent can improve its orchestration from its own interaction history, without parameter updates. We present SpatialCraft, a self-evolving framework that maintains two forms of external knowledge: Experiences, condition-action tactics distilled by contrasting rollouts of the same task, and Skills, multi-step procedures with explicit activation and termination conditions. Three designs couple the two streams. Experiences can be anchored to a Skill, appearing only while it is active rather than once per task. A Contrastive Utility Score estimates each Experience's effect by randomly withholding it across rollouts of the same task, separating its contribution from task difficulty, and Experiences with consistently positive utility are consolidated into the Skills they support. Across five spatial benchmarks and four backbones, SpatialCraft achieves the best accuracy in all 20 settings, showing that a frozen agent can learn to orchestrate spatial tools from its own experience.

papers.title_en: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
papers.authors: Innata Team, Yu Bai, Ziyi Bai, Yuxuan Cai, Chenrui He, Wenhao Li, Zhe Lin, Heng Wang, Hai Yuan, Zhiwei Yu, Yuanhang Zhang, Luyou Chen, Tiezhu Gao, Zheng Geng, Jinbang Guo, Dongxu Han, Diqi He, Börje F. Karlsson, Jintao Li, Zhiyu Li, Xiongkun Linghu, Guang Liu, You Liu, Zhen Luo, Mengsi Lyu, Yufeng Lyu, Zheng Lyu, Quanyue Ma, Chunlei Men, Ziqiang Ni, Tengfei Pan, Yijun Shen, Liang Sun, Shaoxuan Xie, Xiang Yang, Guocai Yao, Hongjun Zhang, Yingli Zhao, Yonghua Lin, Zhongyuan Wang, Huan Yang
papers.evidence: 联合设计具身世界-行动模型与智能体，智能体利用记忆进行长程执行。
papers.tldr: 物理世界开放、动态且部分可观测，单一基础模型难以完成长时程具身执行，模型与智能体的简单集成又易导致规划与控制不一致。为此，Innata-0提出模型-智能体协同设计，构建三塔混合Transformer的世界-行动模型（Innata-0-WAM）和具备记忆、验证、恢复机制的智能体（Innata-0-Agent）。实验结果显示，该系统在理解、世界预测和机器人操作等任务上表现出强大具身能力，成为迈向物理智能的重要第一步。
papers.abstract_en: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery. A co-design protocol is further proposed to align model training with agent execution and leverage validated experiences to support subsequent adaptation and model improvement. Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation. Innata-0 represents our first step toward physical intelligence, and we see it as the beginning of a much longer journey.
